review_candidates.description: About The Position CIVIC’s US Program promotes the adoption of US government policies that help to track, prevent, mitigate, and respond to harm experienced by civilians in armed conflict. Our primary focus includes prevention and accountability for civilian harm related to US military operations, security cooperation activities, and conventional arms transfers. We also lead and work closely in coalitions and campaigns to strengthen transparency, accountability, and oversight of US national security policies and practices. The US Advocacy Advisor will support an ambitious program of work that includes advocacy, research, and cross-organizational coordination with other CIVIC programs and country offices. The Advisor will lead projects and initiatives around US use of force, security cooperation, and civilian harm, including engaging in public and private direct and coalition-based advocacy; leading civil society coalitions; conducting advocacy-relevant research and analysis; coordinating project events; publishing policy briefs, reports, and op-eds; and representing CIVIC to external audiences, US policymakers, and the media. This position requires independence, versatility, tact, and strong communication and project management skills. The ideal candidate enjoys variety in their daily work; embraces innovation; excels at relationship and trust building with diverse stakeholders; can write clearly and succinctly; is detail oriented with an eye for big picture; is able to communicate effectively with peers and supervisors and “manage up”; and while professional at all times, is comfortable with and committed to advocating on behalf of people and communities affected by conflict. This is a full-time role based in Washington, DC on a hybrid work schedule. Washington-based employees are expected to be in CIVIC’s northwest DC office twice weekly. In-person meetings elsewhere in Washington, DC are frequent. The Advisor reports to the US Director. Opportunities may arise for 5–10% travel. Application Deadline: September 29, 2026 Salary and Benefits The salary range for this position is $76,014–$93,116 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications. CIVIC offers a comprehensive benefits package, including employer-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and disability insurance; a flexible leave package; and a 403(b)-retirement savings plan with employer-matched contributions of up to 5% of salary. Key Functions Conducts and supports policy and legal research and analysis for US program outputs and advocacy, including drafting of formal reports, articles, briefs, and advocacy products. Advocates to and educates the US government, including executive branch and Congress, regarding the protection of civilians and security cooperation. Leads, coordinates, and/or supports civil society coalitions to achieve US Program objectives. Conducts policy and legal review of CIVIC US and coalition products. Conducts analysis of legal texts, policy documents, and norms relevant to the job function. Arranges and participates in (or prepares the US Director for) meetings and events with government officials, Congressional staff, and others. Represents CIVIC and the US Program in public and private fora, including public events and with the media; Coordinates social and traditional media strategy and content and the dissemination plans for outputs with the CIVIC Communications team. Develops and maintains working level contacts in government and with other organizations. Attends external (coalition and campaign meetings) and internal meetings on behalf of the US program. Tracks US policy developments in select conflict-affected countries and coordinates meetings with officials on behalf of other CIVIC programs. Builds capacity of CIVIC staff to implement best practices in area of expertise. As required, assists with relevant program management tasks, including contributing to monitoring evaluation, and learning and monthly reporting and assisting with program fundraising and grant writing. Requirements & Qualifications MA/MS or JD degree or equivalent (JD preferred) in law, international affairs, human rights, public policy, security studies, or related fields and at least 5 years of relevant work experience in policy advocacy, human rights, humanitarian affairs, foreign policy, protection of civilians, or related areas. Considerable demonstrated knowledge, expertise, and experience with US foreign and national security policy and law, human rights, civilian protection, and/or international law. Considerable demonstrated knowledge, expertise, and experience with US government policy advocacy, including familiarity with advocacy tools/approaches and experience engaging with US government officials (e.g., executive branch, Congress) to achieve advocacy goals. Experience and familiarity with the civil society landscape engaging in advocacy on US foreign policy. Demonstrated high standard of professional ethics and integrity; treats colleagues and others with dignity and respect and exhibits motivation and personal commitment. Excellent interpersonal communication skills; ability to collaborate and communicate openly across teams. Proven ability to introduce new ways of thinking and doing business into an organization. Understanding of program lifecycle and optimal points to provide advice and support to strengthen US Program / CIVIC and ways of doing business, consistent with best practices in our field. review_candidates.description: Overview WJCF is an Indian non-profit organisation committed to saving lives by reducing the burden of disease and strengthening government-owned, high-quality health systems. Since 2007, WJCF has combined data-driven approaches and deep public health expertise with strong government partnerships to design, implement, and scale solutions across India’s national and state health programmes. We work for and at the service of governments — supporting the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and State Departments of Health to build systems that are strong, sustainable, and led by Indian institutions. As an Indian organisation, WJCF brings an unmatched depth of contextual understanding of India’s health system architecture, policy landscape, and implementation realities across diverse geographies and population groups. This local institutional credibility, combined with global technical rigour, is central to WJCF’s effectiveness as a partner to governments and donors. Our work is built around four complementary roles: as a Trusted Government Partner, co-designing programmes and strengthening health system architecture; as an Operational Partner, translating strategies into effective on-the-ground delivery; as a Market Shaper, improving the availability and affordability of health commodities; and as an Ecosystem Catalyst, convening governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector to drive solutions at scale. WJCF’s programme portfolio spans thematic areas like hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases), syphilis, cervical cancer, diabetes, maternal and childhood anaemia, immunisation, under-5 diarrhoea and pneumonia, sexual and reproductive health, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri – Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), hypoxemia and oxygen, safe drinking water, sickle cell disease, presbyopia, lead poisoning, and cross cutting thematic areas like AI and Health, integrated disease surveillance, and climate and health. We currently support programmes across 19 states and union territories, with teams working at national, state, district, and sub-district levels. Our people are our greatest asset. WJCF brings together a talented, diverse team of professionals from public health, analytics, consulting, healthcare, the development sector, and academia, all united by a shared commitment to improving health outcomes for the people of India. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and deeply grounded in the communities and systems we work in. Our field teams collectively bring hundreds of years of experience managing public health programmes across the country. WJCF collaborates with a range of international and domestic partners and donors to advance its mission, including an affiliation with the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), a global health organisation with which WJCF shares a common mission and values. Program Overview Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is an auto-immune condition characterized by reduced ability to produce insulin in the body, leading to a lifetime dependence on insulin for survival. The condition is associated with a significant strain and poor quality of life and leading to a high financial burden for people living with Type 1 Diabetes (PLT1D) and their families. However, with access to timely diagnostic, initiation on treatment and proper management of the condition, people living with T1D can lead healthy and productive lives, while achieving life expectancy comparable to the general population. There are an estimated 9.4 million PLT1D globally, with India having the second highest share accounting for 8%-10% of the global prevalence. However, nearly 18% of children and adolescents with T1D (~0.3 million) live in India, the highest in the world. The incidence of T1D in the 0-19 age group is increasing more than any other age group. The estimated global incidence of T1D in the 0-19 age group was 8.15 per 100,000 in 2024 and is estimated to increase to 13.95 per 100,000 by 2040. While the burden of T1D has continued to rise over the years, survival has remained poor. Survival rates for children and adolescents with T1D in India is worse compared to countries with similar socio-economic development. On average, in India, PLT1D is estimated to lose approximately 42 healthy years of life due to the combined effects of premature mortality, illness, and disability associated with the condition. There is an urgent need to strengthen access to services and care for T1D. WJCF’s T1D program aims at strengthening and improving access to quality T1D care in India, with the overall goal of achieving longer, healthier, and more productive lives for PLT1D. The program aims to address critical barriers to access and delivery of quality T1D care in India by building awareness, improving access to detection, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up services and care, enabling treatment adherence and self-management, and strengthening governance and policy framework for delivery of T1D care. resolve stock-outs Oversee PLT1D enrolment and follow-up processes — keep the PLT1D registry current, track scheduled follow-up visits, and drive tracing and re-engagement of PLT1Ds lost to follow-up activities across schools, communities, and health facilities in coordination with the state team Monitoring, Reporting, and Quality Assurance Contribute to performance management, capacity-building,
